note: Original random tables for the natural world: forage, mining, wildlife, harvest and building contents. Rows cover each die span exactly once. Written for Asetheria; no third-party text.

entries.name: Forage in the Desert
entries.summary: What a hungry party turns up in the red waste: dates, resin, truffles and a lot of nothing.
entries.body:
Roll once per half-day of foraging in [[Dasht-a Khaliq]]. A successful Survival check earns the roll; a failure earns the last row. Good ground is found at [[The Honey-Palm Oasis]], [[The Myrrh Wadi]] and [[The Truffle Flats]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A handful of dates from a lone [[Honey Palm]]: a day's food for one. |
| 2 | Lumps of hardened gum from a [[Bitter Myrrh]] tree: worth 5 gp to a caravan trader. |
| 3 | A cluster of [[Sand-Truffle]] under a cracked crust: a feast for four. |
| 4 | Wild [[Caravan Cumin]] in a dry wadi: seasons a week of meals. |
| 5 | A stand of salt-bush with edible leaves: poor food, but safe. |
| 6 | A clump of [[Sweet-Root]] the children of the oasis would call a treat. |
| 7 | A hidden seep with clean water and nothing else of use. |
| 8 | Nothing but dust and a scorpion in the boot. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Reroll the last row if the party followed a nomad guide. Truffle-diggers do not share their places.

entries.name: Forage in the Forest
entries.summary: Nuts, bark, berries and fungi of the old forest, and the one mushroom that kills.
entries.body:
Roll once per half-day in [[Foloicauria Forest]]. A Survival check earns the roll. Fungi are best identified at [[The Mushroom Caverns]], and any forager should know the difference before eating.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Acorns from a [[Thunder-Oak]]: bitter but filling when leached. |
| 2 | A thicket of wild berries: a good meal for the whole party. |
| 3 | Bark and leaf of [[Witch Hazel]]: a poultice that eases bruises. |
| 4 | A ring of [[Nullcap (Neutral Mushroom)]]: safe, bland and plentiful. |
| 5 | [[Embergill Bloom (Beneficial Mushroom)]] on a rotting log: a restorative if cooked. |
| 6 | Red-spotted [[Fly-Cap]]: tempting, and a mistake to eat. DC 12 Nature to recognise it. |
| 7 | [[Widow’s Bell (Harmful Mushroom)]], looking very like the safe kind. DC 15 Nature to tell them apart. |
| 8 | A fine day, nothing found, and the sense of being watched. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: On a failed identification check the party eats the row's result. Rows 6 and 7 are poison.

entries.name: Forage in the Marsh
entries.summary: Reeds, roots and leeches of the great marsh, where everything useful is also wet.
entries.body:
Roll once per half-day in [[Maeotis Helos]]. A guide is not optional; see [[The Reed-Cutters' Fen]] for the cutters' channels.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Hollow [[Pen-Reed]], cut and bundled: 2 gp a bundle to a scribe. |
| 2 | A mass of [[River Reed]] fit for thatch or a raft. |
| 3 | A pond of [[Blue Water-Lotus]]: edible roots and a temple's incense. |
| 4 | A jar's worth of [[Healer's Leech]], alive and hungry. |
| 5 | [[Hedge-Mallow]] on a dry hummock: a soothing tea. |
| 6 | Wild duck eggs in the reeds: food for the party for a day. |
| 7 | [[Moorroot]] on the boggy edge: pretty, and best left alone. |
| 8 | Mud, mosquitoes and a sinking boot: lose one hour. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 7 is a trap for the unwary: Moorroot is harmful when eaten or handled bare-handed.

entries.name: Forage in the Mountains
entries.summary: Thin-air herbs and resins of the high crags, and the cold that comes with them.
entries.body:
Roll once per half-day in the [[Olympus Mountain Range]] or [[Cloudspine Ridge]]. Altitude imposes disadvantage on the Survival check above the tree-line. Good ground is [[The Cedar Stair]] and [[The Ibex Crags]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | [[Hymettan Thyme]] on a sunny slope: fragrant, and a bee-keeper's prize. |
| 2 | A scatter of [[Juniper]] berries: seasoning and a mild medicine. |
| 3 | [[Mountain Spikenard]] in a crevice: a perfumer pays 10 gp a bunch. |
| 4 | Resin from a [[Mountain Cedar]]: seals a wound or a waterskin. |
| 5 | [[Balm of the Hill Country]] on a stony shelf: heals minor cuts. |
| 6 | [[Wolf's-Bane]] in a damp gully: a poison, and a hazard to handle. |
| 7 | A cluster of [[Gout-Crocus]]: a physician's drug, a fool's salad. |
| 8 | Bare rock, a chill wind and a cairn left by someone else. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: A cairn on row 8 can hold a message, a cache or a body. Decide before the roll.

entries.name: Forage on the Coast
entries.summary: Sea-onions, gums and shore plants of the Aeolian coast, with the occasional gift of the tide.
entries.body:
Roll once per half-day along the shore of the [[Aeolus Reach]] or [[Nereid’s Veil]]. See [[The Fig Orchards]] for the cultivated side.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A bulb of [[Sea-Onion]]: a poison for rats and a medicine for the heart. |
| 2 | Tears of [[Weeping Mastic]], chewed for the breath or sold for 3 gp. |
| 3 | Pine-nuts under an [[Umbrella Pine]]: a filling snack. |
| 4 | Pods of the [[Locust-Bean]]: sweet, and a standard ration for pack animals. |
| 5 | Olives from a wild [[Grey Olive]]: bitter, preservable and useful. |
| 6 | A strip of washed-up kelp and shellfish: a meal for four. |
| 7 | A drift of [[Pumice]] stones at the tide-line: free scrubbing. |
| 8 | Stinging jellyfish in the shallows: 1d4 damage and nothing for the pot. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: A storm raises the chance of a wreck on the tide-line. Replace row 6 with salvage if one has passed.

entries.name: Forage on the Plains
entries.summary: Grain, herbs and dye-weeds of the grassland, picked over by a thousand years of farmers.
entries.body:
Roll once per half-day on the [[Latium Plains]] or [[Elysian Plains]]. The best farms are in [[The Rye-Ghost Fields]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Wild [[Old Emmer]] gone to seed: grain for a week, with work. |
| 2 | Barley volunteers from a ruined field: [[Legion Barley]], a day's ration. |
| 3 | [[Yellow Weld]] along a track: a dyer's yellow, 2 gp a bundle. |
| 4 | [[Sweet Marjoram]] on a bank: seasoning and a mild calming tea. |
| 5 | [[Soldier's Nettle]] in a ditch: cooked, a fine soup; raw, a hazard. |
| 6 | [[Rope-Hemp]] in a hedge: fibre for rope, 1 gp a bundle. |
| 7 | A black-eared head of [[Rye-Ghost]]: if eaten, strange dreams. DC 12 Nature to spot it. |
| 8 | A fence, a farmer and a polite request to leave. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 7 can be used as a hook for the village of the third furrow.

entries.name: Mining Strike: Building Stone
entries.summary: What a quarry team brings up from a surface cut, by the day.
entries.body:
Roll once per day of work at a quarry such as [[The Pentelic Terraces]], [[The Travertine Cuts]] or [[The Chalk Downs]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Soft [[Tufa Stone]]: easy to cut, cheap to sell. |
| 2 | Pale [[Tiburtine Stone]]: a builder's staple, 1 gp a block. |
| 3 | Fine white [[Pentelic Marble]]: a temple's choice, 50 gp a block. |
| 4 | Honey-white [[Alabaster]]: for jars and lamps. |
| 5 | Hard grey [[Road Basalt]]: for paving and millstones. |
| 6 | A band of [[Black Flint]]: for blades, sparks and walls. |
| 7 | Grey sand of [[Pozzolana]]: makes mortar that sets under water. |
| 8 | Rotten rock: the face slumps and the day's work is lost. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: On a roll of 8 the DM may ask for a DC 12 Dexterity save against falling stone (1d6).

entries.name: Mining Strike: Metal Vein
entries.summary: What a shaft yields when the miners follow a vein, from copper to the rare silver.
entries.body:
Roll once per week of work at a mine such as [[The Green Gallery]], [[The Silver Drifts]] or [[The Calamine Diggings]]. A skilled foreman adds 1 to the roll.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1-2 | [[Copper]] ore, plentiful and poor: 1 gp per hundredweight. |
| 3 | [[Tin]] in a pocket: the rarer half of bronze. |
| 4 | [[Lead]] in heavy grey lumps: for pipes and sling bullets. |
| 5-6 | [[Iron]] ore in a red seam: the backbone of the League's armies. |
| 7 | [[Calamine]]: the brass-maker's gold-maker. |
| 8 | [[Silver]] in a thin vein: worth the digging. |
| 9 | [[Cinnabar]]: red, valuable and poisonous. |
| 10 | [[Gold]] in a quartz stringer: a small fortune, and a large problem. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: On a 10, the overseer wants a share. On a 1, the crew reports a rock-fall.

entries.name: Mining Strike: Gem Pocket
entries.summary: What a lucky prospector finds in a pocket of coloured stone.
entries.body:
Roll when a prospector reports a pocket at [[The Carnelian Washings]], [[Blue-Vein Pit]] or [[The Turquoise Diggings]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | [[Carnelian]], warm red and easy to engrave. |
| 2 | [[Seal Jasper]], banded and good for a signet. |
| 3 | [[Mountain Crystal]], clear as ice. |
| 4 | [[Desert Emerald]], small, green and valuable. |
| 5 | [[Wine-Red Garnet]], dark and rich. |
| 6 | [[Banded Agate]], layered like a cut onion. |
| 7 | [[Nishapur Turquoise]], robin's-egg blue: the satrap will want it. |
| 8 | [[Lapis]], deep blue, flecked gold: the best find of the season. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Stones from the royal diggings are counted. A character who pockets a find risks the satrap's justice.

entries.name: Mining Strike: Strange Find
entries.summary: What turns up in the odd places where the earth or the sky has done something unusual.
entries.body:
Roll once when digging at a strange site such as [[Smoke-Steps]], [[The Pitch Seep]] or [[The Fallen-Star Shrine]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A lump of [[Brimstone]], yellow and choking. |
| 2 | A glassy chunk of [[Fire-Stone]], warm for days. |
| 3 | A skin of [[Persian Naphtha]]: burns on water. |
| 4 | A crust of [[Natron]], white and caustic. |
| 5 | A scatter of [[Orpiment]] and [[Realgar]]: pretty poisons. |
| 6 | A fist of [[Star Metal]]: the iron that fell from the sky. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: A 6 draws attention from the shrine's priests, who regard the stone as theirs.

entries.name: Wildlife Encounter: Desert
entries.summary: Who or what a party meets on the road through the waste.
entries.body:
Roll once per day or night of travel across [[Dasht-a Khaliq]]. See [[The Onager Plain]] and [[The Cobra Heaps]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A [[Hood-Asp]] sunning on a warm stone. |
| 2 | A buried [[Horned Sand-Viper]]: DC 15 Perception to spot it. |
| 3 | A [[Sand Monitor]] raiding a nest. |
| 4 | A [[Fat-Tail Scorpion]] in the bedding. |
| 5 | A pack of [[Gold-Coat Jackal]] following the caravan at a distance. |
| 6 | A herd of [[Wild Ass of the Waste]], running. |
| 7 | A long train of [[Sand-Ship]], with riders. |
| 8 | [[Sky-Cleaner]] vultures circling something dead. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Rows 1, 2 and 4 are poisonous. Row 8 is a hook: find out what died.

entries.name: Wildlife Encounter: Forest
entries.summary: The beasts of the old forest, from the bison to the beetle.
entries.body:
Roll once per day of travel through [[Foloicauria Forest]]. See [[The Aurochs Glades]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A [[Great Forest Bull]] in a glade: dangerous if approached. |
| 2 | A herd of [[Hill Bison]] crossing the trail. |
| 3 | A [[Mountain Brown Bear]] foraging for berries. |
| 4 | A [[Tusker of the Thicket]] in the undergrowth. |
| 5 | A [[Plateau Wolf]] pack at dusk. |
| 6 | A [[Hill Fallow Deer]] drinking at a stream. |
| 7 | A [[Giant Eagle-Owl]] booming from a high branch. |
| 8 | A swarm of [[Blister Beetle]] on the ash trees. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Rows 1, 3 and 4 are combat risks unless the party backs away. Row 8: DC 12 Con save or blistering.

entries.name: Wildlife Encounter: Mountains
entries.summary: Cats, goats and carrion-eaters of the high country.
entries.body:
Roll once per day in the [[Oros Mountain Range]], [[Olympus Mountain Range]] or on [[The Leopard's Ledge]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A [[Plateau Rock-Leopard]] stalking from above. |
| 2 | A band of [[Cliff-Goat]] on an impossible ledge. |
| 3 | A flock of [[Horned Wild Sheep]] grazing a terrace. |
| 4 | A [[King's Eagle]] riding the updraft. |
| 5 | A [[Bone-Breaker]] dropping a bone to crack it. |
| 6 | A [[Mountain Brown Bear]] at a cave mouth. |
| 7 | A covey of [[Rock-Partridge]] flushing underfoot. |
| 8 | A [[Mountain Honeybee]] hive in a rock face. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: The leopard is rarely seen. A character who sees it has been allowed to.

entries.name: Wildlife Encounter: Marsh
entries.summary: Birds, fish and worse in the reeds.
entries.body:
Roll once per day in [[Maeotis Helos]]. See [[The Pelican Islands]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A flock of [[Bill-Bag Pelican]] fishing in a line. |
| 2 | A [[Grey Crane]] dancing on a mudbank. |
| 3 | A [[Phasian Pheasant]] bursting from cover. |
| 4 | A cloud of leeches: [[Healer's Leech]], in the shallows. |
| 5 | A [[Black-Egg Sturgeon]] rolling in a deep channel. |
| 6 | A [[Flame-Wader]] flock, pink in the dusk. |
| 7 | A [[Great Forest Bull]] wading to the neck. |
| 8 | Mist, silence and a channel that was not here yesterday. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 8 is the marsh's own encounter: a lost party, a missing guide, or a thing in the water.

entries.name: Wildlife Encounter: Coast
entries.summary: What the divers and fishermen meet at the water's edge.
entries.body:
Roll once per outing along the [[Aeolus Reach]] or on [[The Sponge Banks]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A [[Pond-Moray]] in a crevice: a bite that does not let go. |
| 2 | An [[Ink-Fish]] changing colour on the sand. |
| 3 | A bed of [[Purple-Snail]] on the rocks. |
| 4 | A school of [[Dying Mullet]] in the shallows. |
| 5 | A [[Diver's Sponge]] colony worth cutting. |
| 6 | A fall of [[Passage Quail]], exhausted on the shingle. |
| 7 | An [[Aeolian Petrel]] fleeing inland: a storm is near. |
| 8 | A [[The Numbfish]] in the sand: a numbing shock for the barefoot. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 7 means a storm within the hour. A wise captain heads for harbour.

entries.name: Wildlife Encounter: Plains
entries.summary: The grassland's herds, hunters and fliers.
entries.body:
Roll once per day on the [[Malaunian Steppe]] or [[Elysian Plains]]. See [[The Lion Grass]] and [[The Horse Meadows]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A [[Mane-King of the Steppe]], hunting at dawn. |
| 2 | A migrating herd of [[Malaunian Saiga]]. |
| 3 | A wild [[Heavenly Horse]] herd: a fortune if one can be caught. |
| 4 | A [[Plateau Wolf]] pack on the edge of the grass. |
| 5 | A pair of [[Two-Hump Camel]] with riders. |
| 6 | A [[Hunting Falcon]] stooping on a hare. |
| 7 | A [[Spring-Swallow]] flock skimming the grass. |
| 8 | A [[Grey Crane]] pair dancing in the wet. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 3 invites a chase. A caught foal is worth a village.

entries.name: Harvest Quality: Plants
entries.summary: How good a gathered crop of herbs, resin or fibre turns out to be.
entries.body:
Roll after a gathering check, adding the character's proficiency bonus. Applies to the plants of [[The Hedge of Healing]], [[The Myrrh Wadi]], [[The Saffron Terraces]] and the like.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 2 | Ruined: spoiled in the gathering, worth nothing. |
| 3-4 | Poor: half the usual yield, half the usual effect. |
| 5-6 | Meagre: three-quarters of the usual yield. |
| 7 | Fair: the usual yield and effect. |
| 8-9 | Good: the usual yield, and the effect lasts twice as long. |
| 10-11 | Fine: a third more than the usual yield at full effect. |
| 12 | Exceptional: double yield and double effect, and word gets round. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Poison or medicine alike: quality scales the dose.

entries.name: Harvest Quality: Hides and Carcasses
entries.summary: What a skinner takes from a kill, from ruined to royal.
entries.body:
Roll after a skinning check on any animal in the codex's fauna list, such as the [[Plateau Rock-Leopard]] or [[Mane-King of the Steppe]]; the best skinners work at [[The Hunting Park]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Ruined: a bad cut and a lost day. |
| 2 | Poor: patchy, fit for rough use only. |
| 3 | Fair: sold at the market rate. |
| 4 | Good: sold at a quarter above the market rate. |
| 5 | Fine: a tanner pays double. |
| 6 | Superb: a gift for a lord, and a story to go with it. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: A kill from a protected species (stork, owl, geese, the temple snakes) brings its own consequences.

entries.name: Harvest Quality: Smelting Yield
entries.summary: How much usable metal a furnace gives from a charge of ore.
entries.body:
Roll once per charge at a furnace such as [[The Copper Smelts]] or [[The Iron Furnaces]]. A master smith adds 2.

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 2 | Slag: the charge is wasted and the furnace needs repair. |
| 3-4 | A third of the expected metal, brittle. |
| 5-6 | Two-thirds of the expected metal. |
| 7-8 | The expected yield. |
| 9-10 | The expected yield, of high quality. |
| 11 | A fifth more than expected, of high quality. |
| 12 | A master-quality ingot, and a reputation for the smith. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: On a 2, the furnace is out of use for a day while the crew rakes the slag.

entries.name: What's in the Gallery
entries.summary: What a party finds in a worked mine gallery, by the shift.
entries.body:
Roll once per chamber explored in a mine such as [[The Green Gallery]], [[The Salt Cathedral]] or [[The Cinnabar Shafts]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Rusted picks and a pile of rubble. |
| 2 | A cold lamp and a miner's lunch, long abandoned. |
| 3 | A seam of the main ore, ready to be cut. |
| 4 | A cistern of foul water. |
| 5 | A rope-ladder to a deeper level. |
| 6 | A crude shrine to the miners' saint, with coins. |
| 7 | A collapsed side-tunnel and a skeleton. |
| 8 | A sealed door, scratched with warnings. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 8 is the entrance to a deeper dungeon. The scratch-marks are the foremen's.

entries.name: What's on the Market Stall
entries.summary: What a stallholder has laid out, from the common to the odd.
entries.body:
Roll once per stall visited at a market such as [[The Spice Wharf]], [[The Amber Stalls]] or [[The Lyre-Makers' Row]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Bundles of common herbs and spices. |
| 2 | Dried figs, almonds and pine-nuts by the bag. |
| 3 | Small cut stones and trinkets. |
| 4 | Dyed cloth in madder-red and woad-blue. |
| 5 | A stack of honey jars with the beekeepers' seal. |
| 6 | Pens, ink and quires of paper. |
| 7 | Cheap amber, probably glass. |
| 8 | A rare item: a potion, a poison or a stone of strange origin. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 7 is a scam. A DC 14 Investigation reveals it.

entries.name: What's in the Common Room
entries.summary: Who is drinking in the inn when the party walks in.
entries.body:
Roll when the party enters an inn such as [[The Wise Owl Inn]], [[The Caravan Stone]] or the keeper's house at [[The Wreckers' Beacon]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A few quiet locals and a sleeping dog. |
| 2 | A caravan crew, loud and homeward bound. |
| 3 | A pair of soldiers off duty, nursing their cups. |
| 4 | A scholar with a book and a candle. |
| 5 | A priest collecting for a shrine. |
| 6 | A story-teller about to begin. |
| 7 | A stranger in a corner, watching the door. |
| 8 | A fight about to start over a dice game. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 7 is the stranger who knows more than he should. Give him a name.

entries.name: What's in the Smithy
entries.summary: What hangs on the wall and sits on the anvil when the party visits a forge.
entries.body:
Roll when the party visits a forge such as [[The Iron Furnaces]] or [[The Cold Forge]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | Horseshoes and nails in tidy bins. |
| 2 | A half-finished plough-blade. |
| 3 | A rack of ordinary swords, priced to move. |
| 4 | Bars of bronze and brass awaiting an order. |
| 5 | A masterwork blade, not for sale. |
| 6 | An apprentice, red-faced, pumping the bellows. |
| 7 | A broken arming sword in for repair, with a noble crest. |
| 8 | A locked chest, and a smith who changes the subject. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 8 is a hook. The chest holds an unfinished commission someone does not want delivered.

entries.name: What's in the Shrine
entries.summary: What a pilgrim finds when they step into a small sanctuary.
entries.body:
Roll when the party enters a shrine such as [[The Fallen-Star Shrine]], [[The Gods' Table Grotto]] or [[The Dream Dormitory]].

| Roll | Result |
|---|---|
| 1 | A lamp, a dish of oil and an empty bench. |
| 2 | Wilted flowers and a scattering of coins. |
| 3 | A priest sweeping the floor. |
| 4 | A family at prayer for a sick child. |
| 5 | Offerings of grain, honey and wine. |
| 6 | A carved wall of names, the dead of the parish. |
| 7 | A hidden niche with a scroll. |
| 8 | A faint light that is not from the lamp. |
entries.dmNotes: Use: Row 8 is the shrine's god taking notice. Decide what the party was asking for.
